---
title: "PROC PRINT"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

PROC PRINT lists the observations of a data set. sasonr writes the listing as
text laid out at `LINESIZE`, and the
table in the HTML or RTF document when one of those destinations is open. The
examples use one small invented data set.

```{r}
prog <- "
options nocenter;
data vitals;
  input subj $ arm $ visit sbp dbp;
  label sbp = 'Systolic BP' dbp = 'Diastolic BP';
  datalines;
S01 A 1 128 82
S01 A 2 124 80
S02 A 1 135 88
S02 A 2 131 85
S03 B 1 118 76
S03 B 2 121 79
;
run;
"
```

## A plain listing

The `Obs` column numbers the observations; numbers without a format are
right-aligned and the column headings are centred over their columns.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## VAR, ID and NOOBS

`VAR` chooses and orders the columns; `ID` replaces the `Obs` column by a
variable; `NOOBS` drops it.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals; id subj; var visit sbp dbp; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## Labels and SPLIT=

`LABEL` uses the variable labels as headings. A label wider than its column is
split at blanks; `SPLIT=` names the character where the heading breaks.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals noobs label; var subj sbp dbp; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## BY groups, SUM and N

With `BY` the data must be sorted by the BY variables; each group gets its BY
line. `SUM` adds the group totals and the grand total.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=vitals; by arm; run;
proc print data=vitals noobs;
  by arm;
  var subj visit sbp;
  sum sbp;
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

`N` writes the number of observations of each group.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=vitals; by arm; run;
proc print data=vitals noobs n;
  by arm;
  var subj sbp;
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## Tables wider than the line

The gap between columns is 4 blanks, or 3, 2, 1 when that makes the table fit
on the line. When it does not fit with a gap of 1, variable names wider than
one-position values are written down the columns; otherwise the columns are
split into panels, each panel repeating the `ID` column.

```{r}
wide <- paste0("options nocenter ls=64; data w; length ",
               paste(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), collapse = " "), " $8; ",
               paste0(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), "='xxxxxx';", collapse = " "),
               " run; proc print data=w noobs; run;")
cat(sas_run(wide)$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## PROC PRINT as an R call

The translation of the program writes each PROC PRINT step as one call of
`sas_proc_print()`, and `sas_run()` runs that same call. Options of the PROC
statement are arguments (`noobs = TRUE`, `split = "*"`), each statement is an
argument named after it: variable names (`var = c(subj, sbp)`), a named
vector for FORMAT (`format = c(sbp = "5.1")`), and `sas_expr()` for the WHERE
condition, which follows the SAS rules (`where = sas_expr("sbp > 125")`).
A data set with data set options is `sas_dataset("vitals", keep = c(subj, sbp))`.

```{r}
res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals noobs label; var subj sbp; where sbp > 125; run;"))
script <- sas_script(res)
cat(tail(as.character(script), 3), sep = "\n")
```

The same call works in a session of your own:

```{r}
s <- sas_session()
invisible(sas_run(prog, session = s))
s |> sas_proc_print(data = "vitals", noobs = TRUE, var = c(subj, visit, sbp), where = sas_expr("sbp > 125"))
cat(sas_listing(s), sep = "\n")
```

## The RTF document

PROC PRINT has no HTML view yet; under `ODS RTF FILE="path";` its table goes
into an RTF document in the default RTF style (heading row repeated on every
page, BY lines, tables wider than the page split into column groups), written
at `ODS RTF CLOSE;`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sas_run(paste(prog, "
ods rtf file=\"vitals.rtf\";
proc print data=vitals noobs label; var subj visit sbp dbp; run;
ods rtf close;"))
```

## What fails loud

sasonr stops with a `sasonr_unsupported` condition, naming the SAS line, for
the layouts it does not implement yet, for example column panels with more
than one observation, BY groups or `SUM`, and the page headers of a listing
longer than one page under a small `PAGESIZE=`.

```{r, error = TRUE}
sas_run(paste0("options nocenter ls=64; data w; length ",
               paste(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), collapse = " "), " $8; ",
               paste0(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), "='xxxxxx';", collapse = " "),
               " output; output; run; proc print data=w noobs; run;"))
```
